title: Record genre changes field-role distribution
summary: Test whether a candidate whole's semantic role differs between description records and instruction records, rather than assuming one portable translation across genres.

design.mechanism: The same whole may be a property/state marker in descriptive records but a procedure-condition marker in instructions because genre supplies a bounded role frame.
design.unit: complete candidate occurrences in independently classified description and instruction records
design.contrast: genre-stratified role distributions with leave-one-record-out validation, controlling register and position
design.prediction: A candidate shows a reproducible role interaction with genre, while its neighboring field types remain within each genre; a single portable meaning predicts no interaction.
design.falsifier: No held-record genre interaction, or the interaction disappears under record-level controls, falsifies the genre-conditioned role claim.
design.scope: cached admitted record classifications and exact whole occurrences; endpoint availability_unknown for independent genre labels
design.related: Existing q13 record-schema histories are broad comparators, not this candidate-level genre interaction; no decoder or regex-only test is proposed
